title: Excelsior marches; Willie Humphrey and John Casimir on clarinet
summary: Excelsior marches, Peter and Charlie Love leading; Willie Humphrey's strong clarinet and John Casimir squealing, with the raw-egg story.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, that was the way where they take the Excelsior, now the Excelsior brass band, they had some beautiful marches, and, well, Peter sometime would be playing a tune in or something. Well, Peter would get out the band, and coming back, second line, if you call him, coming on back from the graveyard, Peter would get out, because he knew he had to go play. Well, Charlie Love would take over. Well, Willie Ompford said, if you asked him now, Pete didn't lie all that. Yeah. See? And God dang it, they'd knock off hard society, and Willie put that clarinet up there, and God dang it, you could hear him from the next corner's house. Yeah.
Could hear him from the other way down the next corner with that clarinet.
Yeah, Willie was a strong man, on the play. John Cappie was strong going clarinet, too.

Yeah, he could squeal. Yeah, he squeal like I don't know what with that clarinet. Yeah. He used to make me laugh with a lady up in Kenna. They called her Miss Cus, which they go play for on Saturday night. So, John would come in and say, Miss Cus, she said, what is it, John? I said, you got any raw eggs? She said, yeah, John. I said, give me two. John would take two of them raw eggs, and he'd suck them down, and he'd tell those red olives, and I'm going to blow you off the bandstand for the night. I don't know.
He'd suck the raw eggs, then.
